description:
We are a team of six passionate Sri Lankan student developers building a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer an interactive and engaging web application that brings space exploration to life through exciting missions, knowledge-based quizzes featuring real NASA facts, and achievement-based rewards such as badges and certificates.

Our goal is to make space education more engaging, accessible, and enjoyable while inspiring curiosity, creativity, and a passion for science and technology.
summary:
We built AstroBase, a browser-based training platform that lets people explore astronaut training and space missions, no matter where they live. Experiencing astronaut training normally requires specialized facilities and equipment, and we wanted to help lower that barrier.

AstroBase brings interactive 3D simulations, structured training modules, mission planning tools, and space science resources together in one place. Users can practice simulated spacewalks, work through emergency situations, operate planetary rovers, and learn about the challenges astronauts face on real missions.

We incorporated real NASA data, including space weather information from DONKI and radiation research datasets from OSDR, so scientific information becomes something people can explore, understand, and learn from.

We believe an interest in space should not depend on money or access. Whether you are a student, a curious kid, or someone who dreams of exploring space, AstroBase gives you a way to learn, experiment, and discover. Our goal is to inspire the next generation of space explorers.
details:
AstroBase is a training platform that runs in the browser. It lets you explore astronaut training and space missions without needing a real training facility. We built it for students, space fans, and anyone who has ever wondered what it takes to become an astronaut.

There’s a lot inside it. It has an eight-module training course, 3D simulations, a mission planning workspace, a space science lab, a training dashboard, and communication tools based on how real missions work. You can experience a simulated spacewalk, deal with an emergency, or drive a rover across a planet.

The biggest benefit is that you don’t need anything special to start. Open a browser and start exploring astronaut training. You learn by doing, not just by reading. We also use NASA scientific resources, including DONKI for space weather information and OSDR for space radiation research, so what you learn is connected to actual space science.

We want more people to be able to learn about space, wherever they live. If AstroBase makes someone curious about space science or engineering, that’s a win for us.

For the technology, the frontend uses React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS. The 3D parts use Three.js and React Three Fiber. The backend is ASP.NET Core with C#, Supabase PostgreSQL stores the data, and the frontend and backend communicate through REST APIs.

What makes AstroBase special is that it brings everything together in one place. Training, simulations, mission planning, and scientific resources are all available through a single website, allowing users to take part in simulated mission experiences instead of just reading about them.

While building it, we thought about ease of use, educational value, and how well the simulations perform in a browser. We also left room for future improvements, including AI-powered mission guidance and VR training.
